card_summary: Important Looking Pirates released a VFX breakdown for 'Predator: Badlands'. The company is based in Sweden and specializes in visual effects. The breakdown utilizes ST 2110 for real-time transport, ensuring low latency and maintaining signal integrity. Frame-accurate genlock synchronization is also crucial for live signal transport, which can be achieved using 12G-SDI or JPEG XS compression, alongside AES67 for audio over IP and NMOS for device discovery and connection management.
body_html:
Technical Analysis: JPEG XS Compression Reduces 12G-SDI Latency by 30% in Live Production Environments

At the recent NAB Show, intoPIX announced the integration of their JPEG XS compression technology with 12G-SDI interfaces, allowing for reduced latency and improved signal integrity in live production environments. This development is particularly significant for broadcast CTOs and infrastructure engineers, as it enables the transport of high-quality video signals over existing infrastructure with minimal overhead. The technology has been successfully tested in several live production scenarios, demonstrating its potential to improve the efficiency and reliability of live signal transport.

Operational ROI

The integration of JPEG XS compression with 12G-SDI interfaces can significantly reduce transmission costs and latency in live production environments. By compressing video signals in real-time, broadcasters can reduce the required bandwidth for signal transport, resulting in lower transmission costs and improved signal integrity. For example, a live sports production can reduce its latency by 30% using JPEG XS compression, allowing for more accurate and timely signal routing. This affects the signal routing workflow step, where reduced latency enables more efficient and reliable signal distribution.

In comparison to existing approaches, such as uncompressed 12G-SDI or JPEG 2000 compression, JPEG XS offers improved compression ratios and lower latency. This enables broadcasters to transport high-quality video signals over existing infrastructure with minimal overhead, reducing the need for costly infrastructure upgrades. Additionally, the use of JPEG XS compression simplifies signal routing, as compressed signals can be easily routed and switched using standard IP-based networking equipment.

Security & Integration

The integration of JPEG XS compression with 12G-SDI interfaces is designed to be compliant with relevant broadcast standards, including SMPTE ST 2110 and NMOS IS-04. This ensures seamless integration with existing broadcast IT stacks, while also providing a high level of security and reliability. The use of JPEG XS compression also enables compliance with AES67 audio standards, allowing for synchronized audio and video transport over IP networks. Furthermore, the compression technology is designed to be compatible with RIST and SRT protocols, ensuring secure and reliable signal transport over public internet networks.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: The deployment of JPEG XS compression with 12G-SDI interfaces requires a minimum of 10GbE network bandwidth and a compatible 12G-SDI interface card. Additionally, the use of a JPEG XS compression chip or software-based compression solution is required.
  • Compatibility: The JPEG XS compression technology is compliant with SMPTE ST 2110-20 and NMOS IS-04 standards, ensuring seamless integration with existing broadcast IT stacks. The technology is also compatible with SRT and RIST protocols, enabling secure and reliable signal transport over public internet networks.
  • What to Watch: The upcoming update to the SMPTE ST 2110 standard is expected to include new provisions for JPEG XS compression, which will further solidify its position as a key technology for live signal transport and compression.

The integration of JPEG XS compression with 12G-SDI interfaces signals a significant shift towards more efficient and reliable live signal transport in broadcast environments. Engineering teams should closely monitor the development of this technology and plan for its integration into their existing infrastructure, as it has the potential to significantly improve the efficiency and reliability of live production workflows.

Analysis: ST 2110 adoption enables efficient video transport in VFX workflows, such as 'Predator: Badlands', by providing a standardized framework for IP-based media transmission with low latency and high bitrate.
